Fourteen findings: five high, six medium, three low. High: (1) Scholze's Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations (ACC Theorems 2.3.5/2.3.7/2.3.8) and the non-Eisenstein notion have no supplier at all - TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure is never cited although it is a declared roadmap prerequisite, and the accepted IHG nodes for Definition 2.3.6 and Lemma 2.2.4 are not used; (7) the twisted action g ·_p x = alpha_lambda(g)^{-1} g x that makes U_{v,i} integral and invertible is assigned to PA.2/iwahori-level-tower but defined nowhere; (8) the ordinary weight algebra Lambda (Lambda_1, the minimal prime wp_0, Lambda_v) is never defined and hypothesis (3) of Theorem 6.6.2 is unused; (9) Proposition 5.4.18 lacks its characteristic-zero ordinary unitary input (Theorem 2.3.3, [Ger19, Lem. 5.4], [Tho15, Th. 2.4], the auxiliary character), whose only planned statement sits downstream in PA's own Part II; (11) the reflection step of Corollary 4.4.8 does not deliver condition (b) (a gap in the published argument, inherited by Theorem 4.5.1(b)). Medium: Theorem 3.1.1 requested from the characteristic-zero stage AG2.5 instead of the IHG Part II the accepted extraction routes it to; Theorem 2.4.11 unsupplied though ALS.5/unitary-middle-degree states it; a stage cycle PA.2/PA.5 <-> PL.0 created by importing a Part II node into the base; missing 'decomposed K~' and §4 standing hypotheses in PA.1; missing internal edges (Lemma 5.3.3 and Lemma 4.3.6 nodes orphaned or unused); no iota-ordinary <-> T^{S,ord} comparison; completed cohomology planned without CompletedCohomologyPartII and Lemma 5.2.14. Low: requests that duplicate exact L8/G8 nodes (one sent to the wrong stage); unit tests that cannot see the shuffle, CTG and rec^T conventions. The baseline citations, the final statements of Theorems 6.1.1/6.1.2, Proposition 6.5.13, the §6.5.1/§6.6.1 hypothesis lists, Lemmas 7.1.1-7.1.3 and the compiled Lean cores were checked and hold.

findings.claim: The unit tests of the two convention-carrying definitions do not catch the conventions they are about (PROTOCOL section 12). (a) KostantShuffle is defined by 'the inverse is increasing on each block' (representatives of left Levi cosets), but every permutation occurring in its four tests is an involution (both permutations of Fin 2, finAddFlip on Fin(n+n), the transposition (0 1)), so the tempting wrong definition 'w itself is increasing on each block' (representatives of W/W_P) passes all four; the review's statement that the tests 'distinguish inverse-increasing left shuffles' is not borne out. (b) CTGWeight compares mu(w,tau,i) + mu(w,tau c, n-1-i) with a constant vector; all three tests have n <= 1 or the zero table, so a definition that drops the reversal i -> n-1-i (lambda_{w,tau c} instead of -lambda^vee_{w,tau c}), or one that uses the difference mu(w,tau,i) - mu(w,tau c,i) (no dual), passes all three (for the latter: the zero table gives constant differences, and in rank_one_pair the differences 1, -1, 0, 0 are not constant, exactly as the sums 1, 1, 0, 0 are not). (c) WeaklyAutomorphicPrimeTo is defined through rec^T_{F_v}(pi_v)(Frob_v) (geometric Frobenius, the arithmetic normalization of Boxer-Calegari-Gee-Newton-Thorne Definition 6.1.2(3)), but its three tests and four API items only exercise the quantifiers over T; a definition using the unitary rec_{F_v} (a shift by |det|^{(1-n)/2}) or arithmetic Frobenius passes all of them, although Lemmas 6.1.3-6.1.4 of that paper depend on the normalization.
findings.evidence: Suggested file (compiled at Mathlib 082e2d3, 92 sorry warnings, no errors): KostantShuffle := {w : Perm (Fin (n+n)) // StrictMono (fun i => w.symm (Fin.castAdd n i)) ∧ StrictMono (fun i => w.symm (Fin.natAdd n i))}; tests rank_one (n = 1), rank_zero (n = 0), block_swap (s.val = finAddFlip, an involution since finAddFlip (castAdd k) = natAdd n k and conversely), internal_swap (Equiv.swap 0 1). CTGWeight c mu := ∀ w a, ∃ τ, (fun i => mu w τ i + mu w (c τ) i.rev) ≠ fun _ => a; tests zero (zero table), empty_w (W empty), rank_one_pair (n = 1). ACC p. 974, Definition 4.3.5: 'for all w in W^P and for all i0 in Z, there exists tau in Hom(F, E) such that lambda_{w,tau} − lambda^vee_{w,tau c} ≠ (i0, i0, ..., i0)'. Counterexamples: for n = 2 the permutation w = [2,0,1,3] (w(0)=2, w(1)=0, w(2)=1, w(3)=3) has w^{-1} = [1,2,0,3], increasing on {0,1} and on {2,3}, so it is a shuffle, of length 2, while w is not increasing on {0,1} and w^{-1} is not a shuffle; for CTG with n = 2, one w and one conjugate pair tau, tau c with mu(tau) = mu(tau c) = (1,0), the reversed sums are (1,1) (not CTG) while the unreversed sums are (2,0) (CTG). PA.5/weak-automorphy-prime-to-set: statement '... pi_v is unramified and rec^T_{F_v}(pi_v)(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial iota(Q_v(X))'; tests 'An automorphic system is weakly automorphic prime to the empty set', 'At T={v0}, a witness must match at v0 ...', 'T∩S≠∅ is inadmissible'.
findings.fix: Add, in the packet and as examples in the suggested file: KostantShuffle.non_involution (for n = 2, the permutation [2,0,1,3] is a shuffle of length 2 and its inverse [1,2,0,3] is not); CTGWeight.reversal (n = 2, one w, embeddings {tau, tau c} with mu(tau) = mu(tau c) = (1,0): not CTG) CTGWeight.sum_not_difference (n = 1, one w, two conjugate pairs a, ac, b, bc with mu(a) = mu(b) = 1 and mu(ac) = mu(bc) = 0: every conjugate sum equals 1, so the table is not CTG, whereas the differences are +1 and -1, so the difference variant would call it CTG); and WeaklyAutomorphicPrimeTo.cyclotomic (n = 1: the cyclotomic system with Q_v(X) = X - q_v^{-1} is witnessed by the norm character |.| and not by |.|^{-1}), which separates geometric from arithmetic Frobenius.
